subject: math
title: Grade 6 Perimeter of Complex Shapes
seo_title: Grade 6 Perimeter of Complex Shapes Worksheets: Free Math Practice with Answer Key (BC Curriculum)
meta_desc: Free Grade 6 math worksheets on the perimeter of complex shapes for the BC curriculum: review rectangles, find missing sides on L and T shapes, multiply for regular polygons, add only the outside of composite shapes, and solve fencing and trail word problems. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: Find every missing side first, then add all the sides around the outside.
key_sub: Whole side − known part = missing part. Rectangle: 2 × (l + w). Regular polygon: side × number of sides. A side where two shapes touch is inside, so leave it out.
body_html:
What is perimeter?

Perimeter is the distance all the way around a shape. To find it, add every outside side. Perimeter is a length, so it uses mm, cm, m or km.

Shortcuts: a rectangle has 2 lengths and 2 widths, so P = 2 × (l + w). A regular polygon has equal sides, so P = side length × number of sides.

L and T shapes: find the missing sides first

When all the corners are square, the sides going right add up to the sides going left, and the sides going down add up to the sides going up. Use this to find each missing side. Then add every side.

Example 1: check with the shortcut

Find the perimeter of the L shape above another way.

An L shape has the same perimeter as the rectangle around it: 2 × (12 + 9) = 2 × 21 = 42.

Answer: 42 m, the same answer

Composite shapes: only the outside counts

When shapes are put together, the side where they touch is inside. It is not part of the perimeter.

Example 2: fencing with a gate

A dog run is 15 m long and 8 m wide. The 1.5 m gate is not fence. How much fence is needed?

Perimeter: 2 × (15 + 8) = 46 m. Take away the gate: 46 − 1.5 = 44.5.

Answer: 44.5 m

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Missing a side, often a short one on an L or T shapeCount the sides first, then check that you added that many numbers
Using the wrong length for a missing side (the whole side instead of the part)Find the parallel sides. Whole side − known part = missing part
Adding only the numbers shownFind the missing sides first, then add every side
Counting a side where two shapes touchThat side is inside. Only the outside counts
Adding 3 m + 45 cm as 48Change to one unit first: 300 cm + 45 cm

faq.q: What do Grade 6 students learn about perimeter in BC?
faq.a: In the Geometry and measurement area of the BC Grade 6 math curriculum, students find the perimeter of complex shapes, such as L and T shapes, regular polygons and shapes made of rectangles and triangles.

faq.q: How do you find the perimeter of an L-shaped figure?
faq.a: Find each missing side by subtracting the known part from the whole side across from it, then add all 6 sides. As a check, an L shape has the same perimeter as the rectangle around it.

faq.q: How do you find the perimeter of a regular polygon?
faq.a: Multiply the side length by the number of sides. A regular hexagon with 2.5 cm sides has a perimeter of 6 × 2.5 = 15 cm.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake with complex shapes?
faq.a: Missing a short side or using the whole side for a missing part. Count the sides first, find every missing length, and then add them all.

items.q: What is the perimeter of the rectangle?
items.e: A rectangle has 2 lengths and 2 widths: 2 × 14 + 2 × 9 = 28 + 18 = 46 cm. 14 + 9 = 23 is only two of the four sides.

items.q: What is the perimeter of the rectangle?
items.e: A rectangle has 2 lengths and 2 widths: 2 × 23 + 2 × 17 = 46 + 34 = 80 m. 23 + 17 = 40 is only two of the four sides.

items.q: What is the perimeter of the rectangle?
items.e: A rectangle has 2 lengths and 2 widths: 2 × 8.5 + 2 × 4 = 17 + 8 = 25 cm. 8.5 + 4 = 12.5 is only two of the four sides.

items.q: What is the perimeter of the rectangle?
items.e: A rectangle has 2 lengths and 2 widths: 2 × 12.5 + 2 × 7.5 = 25 + 15 = 40 m. 12.5 + 7.5 = 20 is only two of the four sides.

items.q: What is the perimeter of the rectangle?
items.e: A rectangle has 2 lengths and 2 widths: 2 × 6.4 + 2 × 3.8 = 12.8 + 7.6 = 20.4 cm. 6.4 + 3.8 = 10.2 is only two of the four sides.

items.q: What is the perimeter of the rectangle?
items.e: A rectangle has 2 lengths and 2 widths: 2 × 145 + 2 × 90 = 290 + 180 = 470 m. 145 + 90 = 235 is only two of the four sides.

items.q: What is the perimeter of the rectangle?
items.e: A rectangle has 2 lengths and 2 widths: 2 × 2.75 + 2 × 1.5 = 5.5 + 3 = 8.5 m. 2.75 + 1.5 = 4.25 is only two of the four sides.

items.q: What is the perimeter of the rectangle?
items.e: A rectangle has 2 lengths and 2 widths: 2 × 36 + 2 × 24 = 72 + 48 = 120 m. 36 + 24 = 60 is only two of the four sides.

items.q: This is a square. What is its perimeter?
items.e: All 4 sides of a square are equal: 4 × 13.5 = 54 cm. 2 × 13.5 = 27 counts only two sides.

items.q: This is a square. What is its perimeter?
items.e: All 4 sides of a square are equal: 4 × 48 = 192 m. 2 × 48 = 96 counts only two sides.

items.q: A rectangle is l long and w wide. Which expression gives its perimeter?
items.e: Add one length and one width, then double it, because there are two of each: 2 × (l + w). This is the same as 2 × l + 2 × w. l × w is the area.

items.q: Olivia finds the perimeter of a rectangle 12 m long and 5 m wide like this: 2 × 12 + 5 = 29 m. What went wrong?
items.e: 2 × 12 counts both lengths, but + 5 adds only one width. The rectangle has two 5 m widths: 2 × 12 + 2 × 5 = 24 + 10 = 34 m.

items.q: What is the perimeter of the rectangle in centimetres?
items.e: The units are different. Change first: 3 m = 300 cm. Then 2 × 300 + 2 × 45 = 600 + 90 = 690 cm. 96 mixes m and cm.

items.q: What is the perimeter of the rectangle in centimetres?
items.e: The units are different. Change first: 1.2 m = 120 cm. Then 2 × 120 + 2 × 80 = 240 + 160 = 400 cm. 162.4 mixes m and cm.

items.q: What is the perimeter of the rectangle in metres?
items.e: The units are different. Change first: 2 km = 2000 m. Then 2 × 2000 + 2 × 750 = 4000 + 1500 = 5500 m. 1504 mixes km and m.

items.q: What is the perimeter of the rectangle in millimetres?
items.e: The units are different. Change first: 25 cm = 250 mm. Then 2 × 250 + 2 × 60 = 500 + 120 = 620 mm. 170 mixes cm and mm.

items.q: The perimeter of the rectangle is 58 cm. How wide is it?
items.e: The two lengths use 2 × 17 = 34 cm. That leaves 58 − 34 = 24 cm for the two widths. Each width is 24 ÷ 2 = 12 cm.

items.q: The perimeter of the rectangle is 19 m. How wide is it?
items.e: The two lengths use 2 × 6.5 = 13 m. That leaves 19 − 13 = 6 m for the two widths. Each width is 6 ÷ 2 = 3 m.

items.q: The perimeter of the rectangle is 1000 m. How wide is it?
items.e: The two lengths use 2 × 320 = 640 m. That leaves 1000 − 640 = 360 m for the two widths. Each width is 360 ÷ 2 = 180 m.

items.q: A rectangular farm in the Fraser Valley is 3250 m long and 2175 m wide. What is its perimeter?

sets.title: L and T shapes: find the missing sides

items.q: All the corners are square corners. What is the length of side x?
items.e: Look at the sides that run the same way as x. The whole side is 11 cm, and the other part is 7 cm. So x = 11 − 7 = 4 cm. Using 11 cm for x uses the whole side, not the part.

items.q: All the corners are square corners. What is the length of side x?
items.e: x is the whole side. It is made of the parts across from it: 5 + 3 = 8 m. Subtracting the parts gives the wrong length.

items.q: All the corners are square corners. What is the perimeter of the shape?
items.e: First find the missing sides: 12 − 9 = 3 and 10 − 6 = 4. Then add all 6 sides: 12 + 4 + 9 + 6 + 3 + 10 = 44 cm. 37 cm is only the sides with numbers. Shortcut: an L shape has the same perimeter as the rectangle around it, 2 × (12 + 10) = 44.

items.q: All the corners are square corners. What is the perimeter of the shape?
items.e: First find the missing sides: 10 − 4 = 6 and 8 − 5 = 3. Then add all 6 sides: 6 + 5 + 4 + 3 + 10 + 8 = 36 m. 27 m is only the sides with numbers. Shortcut: an L shape has the same perimeter as the rectangle around it, 2 × (10 + 8) = 36.

items.q: All the corners are square corners. What is the length of side x?
items.e: Look at the sides that run the same way as x. The whole side is 6.5 m, and the other part is 3.5 m. So x = 6.5 − 3.5 = 3 m. Using 6.5 m for x uses the whole side, not the part.

items.q: All the corners are square corners. What is the length of side x?
items.e: Look at the sides that run the same way as x. The whole side is 18 cm, and the other part is 12 cm. So x = 18 − 12 = 6 cm. Using 18 cm for x uses the whole side, not the part.

items.q: All the corners are square corners. What is the perimeter of the shape?
items.e: First find the missing sides: 30 − 10 = 20 and 22 − 14 = 8. Then add all 6 sides: 30 + 8 + 20 + 14 + 10 + 22 = 104 m. 76 m is only the sides with numbers. Shortcut: an L shape has the same perimeter as the rectangle around it, 2 × (30 + 22) = 104.

items.q: All the corners are square corners. What is the perimeter of the shape?
items.e: First find the missing sides: 5.5 − 2 = 3.5 and 4 − 2.5 = 1.5. Then add all 6 sides: 5.5 + 1.5 + 3.5 + 2.5 + 2 + 4 = 19 cm. 14 cm is only the sides with numbers. Shortcut: an L shape has the same perimeter as the rectangle around it, 2 × (5.5 + 4) = 19.

items.q: All the corners are square corners. What is the length of side x?
items.e: Look at the sides that run the same way as x. The whole side is 14 cm, and the other parts add up to 5 + 3 = 8 cm. So x = 14 − 8 = 6 cm. Using 14 cm for x uses the whole side, not the part.

items.q: All the corners are square corners. What is the perimeter of the shape?
items.e: First find the missing sides: 14 − (6 + 5) = 3 and (4 + 7) − 7 = 4. Then add all 8 sides: 14 + 4 + 6 + 7 + 3 + 7 + 5 + 4 = 50 cm. 43 cm is only the sides with numbers.

items.q: All the corners are square corners. What is the length of side x?
items.e: Look at the sides that run the same way as x. The whole side is 130 cm, and the other part is 80 cm. So x = 130 − 80 = 50 cm. Using 130 cm for x uses the whole side, not the part.

items.q: All the corners are square corners. What is the perimeter of the shape?
items.e: First find the missing sides: 12 − 5 = 7 and 9 − 3 = 6. Then add all 6 sides: 12 + 3 + 5 + 6 + 7 + 9 = 42 cm. 29 cm is only the sides with numbers. Shortcut: an L shape has the same perimeter as the rectangle around it, 2 × (12 + 9) = 42.

items.q: All the corners are square corners. What is the length of side x?
items.e: Look at the sides that run the same way as x. The whole side is 22.5 m, and the other parts add up to 7.5 + 10.5 = 18 m. So x = 22.5 − 18 = 4.5 m. Using 22.5 m for x uses the whole side, not the part.

items.q: All the corners are square corners. What is the perimeter of the shape?
items.e: First find the missing sides: 15 − (4 + 6) = 5 and (7 + 3) − 3 = 7. Then add all 8 sides: 4 + 7 + 5 + 7 + 6 + 3 + 15 + 3 = 50 m. 38 m is only the sides with numbers.

items.q: All the corners are square corners. What is the length of side x?
items.e: Look at the sides that run the same way as x. The whole side is 9 m, and the other part is 5 m. So x = 9 − 5 = 4 m. Using 9 m for x uses the whole side, not the part.

items.q: All the corners are square corners. What is the perimeter of the shape?
items.e: First find the missing sides: 50 + 90 = 140 and 70 + 40 = 110. Then add all 6 sides: 140 + 70 + 50 + 40 + 90 + 110 = 500 m. 250 m is only the sides with numbers. Shortcut: an L shape has the same perimeter as the rectangle around it, 2 × (140 + 110) = 500.

items.q: All the corners are square corners. What is the length of side x?
items.e: Look at the sides that run the same way as x. The whole side is 75 cm, and the other parts add up to 15 + 25 = 40 cm. So x = 75 − 40 = 35 cm. Using 75 cm for x uses the whole side, not the part.

items.q: All the corners are square corners. What is the perimeter of the shape?
items.e: First find the missing sides: 7.5 − (2 + 3) = 2.5 and (4 + 1.5) − 4 = 1.5. Then add all 8 sides: 2 + 4 + 2.5 + 4 + 3 + 1.5 + 7.5 + 1.5 = 26 m. 22 m is only the sides with numbers.

items.q: All the corners are square corners. What is the perimeter of the shape?
items.e: First find the missing sides: 27.5 − 20 = 7.5 and 22.5 − 10 = 12.5. Then add all 6 sides: 27.5 + 12.5 + 20 + 10 + 7.5 + 22.5 = 100 m. 80 m is only the sides with numbers. Shortcut: an L shape has the same perimeter as the rectangle around it, 2 × (27.5 + 22.5) = 100.

items.q: All the corners are square corners. What is the perimeter of the shape?
items.e: First find the missing sides: 45 − (18 + 15) = 12 and (24 + 9) − 24 = 9. Then add all 8 sides: 45 + 9 + 18 + 24 + 15 + 24 + 12 + 9 = 156 cm. 135 cm is only the sides with numbers.

sets.title: Regular polygons: side length × number of sides

items.q: All the sides of this equilateral triangle are the same length. What is its perimeter?
items.e: An equilateral triangle has 3 equal sides. Multiply: 3 × 12.5 = 37.5 cm. 12.5 × 4 = 50 would treat it like a square.

items.q: All the sides of this regular pentagon are the same length. What is its perimeter?
items.e: A regular pentagon has 5 equal sides. Multiply: 5 × 14 = 70 cm. 14 × 4 = 56 would treat it like a square.

items.q: All the sides of this equilateral triangle are the same length. What is its perimeter?
items.e: An equilateral triangle has 3 equal sides. Multiply: 3 × 45 = 135 mm. 45 × 4 = 180 would treat it like a square.

items.q: All the sides of this regular hexagon are the same length. What is its perimeter?
items.e: A regular hexagon has 6 equal sides. Multiply: 6 × 9.5 = 57 cm. 9.5 × 4 = 38 would treat it like a square.

items.q: All the sides of this regular octagon are the same length. What is its perimeter?
items.e: A regular octagon has 8 equal sides. Multiply: 8 × 15 = 120 cm. 15 × 4 = 60 would treat it like a square.

items.q: A regular octagon has a perimeter of 96 cm. Which number sentence finds the length of one side?
items.e: An octagon has 8 equal sides, so share the perimeter into 8 parts: 96 ÷ 8 = 12 cm.

items.q: All the sides of this regular decagon are the same length. What is its perimeter?
items.e: A regular decagon has 10 equal sides. Multiply: 10 × 6 = 60 m. 6 × 4 = 24 would treat it like a square.

items.q: A regular hexagon has a perimeter of 57 cm. How long is each side?
items.e: A regular hexagon has 6 equal sides: 57 ÷ 6 = 9.5 cm. Check: 6 × 9.5 = 57. Dividing by 4 only works for a square.

items.q: All the sides of this regular hexagon are the same length. What is its perimeter?
items.e: A regular hexagon has 6 equal sides. Multiply: 6 × 2.5 = 15 m. 2.5 × 4 = 10 would treat it like a square.

items.q: All the sides of this regular decagon are the same length. What is its perimeter?
items.e: A regular decagon has 10 equal sides. Multiply: 10 × 12.5 = 125 cm. 12.5 × 4 = 50 would treat it like a square.

items.q: All the sides of this regular pentagon are the same length. What is its perimeter?
items.e: A regular pentagon has 5 equal sides. Multiply: 5 × 3.4 = 17 m. 3.4 × 4 = 13.6 would treat it like a square.

items.q: A regular octagon has a perimeter of 100 m. How long is each side?
items.e: A regular octagon has 8 equal sides: 100 ÷ 8 = 12.5 m. Check: 8 × 12.5 = 100. Dividing by 4 only works for a square.

items.q: Which has the longer perimeter: a square with 15 cm sides or a regular hexagon with 10 cm sides?
items.e: Square: 4 × 15 = 60 cm. Hexagon: 6 × 10 = 60 cm. They are the same. 225 is the area of the square, and 70 cm uses 7 sides for the hexagon.

items.q: All the sides of this regular octagon are the same length. What is its perimeter?
items.e: A regular octagon has 8 equal sides. Multiply: 8 × 0.75 = 6 m. 0.75 × 4 = 3 would treat it like a square.

items.q: A regular pentagon has a perimeter of 8.5 m. How long is each side?
items.e: A regular pentagon has 5 equal sides: 8.5 ÷ 5 = 1.7 m. Check: 5 × 1.7 = 8.5. Dividing by 4 only works for a square.

items.q: A regular polygon has sides of 7 cm. Its perimeter is 63 cm. How many sides does it have?
items.e: Number of sides = perimeter ÷ side length: 63 ÷ 7 = 9. It is a regular nonagon. Check: 9 × 7 = 63.

items.q: A regular decagon has a perimeter of 135 cm. How long is each side?
items.e: A regular decagon has 10 equal sides: 135 ÷ 10 = 13.5 cm. Check: 10 × 13.5 = 135. Dividing by 4 only works for a square.

items.q: Each regular polygon below has 6 cm sides. Which one has a perimeter of 48 cm?
items.e: 48 ÷ 6 = 8 sides, so it is a regular octagon. Check: 8 × 6 = 48 cm.

items.q: An equilateral triangle has sides of 1.25 m. What is its perimeter in centimetres?
items.e: 3 × 1.25 = 3.75 m. 1 m = 100 cm, so 3.75 m = 375 cm. 3.75 cm forgets to change metres to centimetres.

items.q: A stop sign is shaped like a regular octagon. Each side is about 30 cm. About how long is the edge all the way around, in metres?
items.e: 8 × 30 = 240 cm. 100 cm = 1 m, so 240 cm = 2.4 m. 1.2 m uses only 4 sides, and 2.1 m uses 7 sides.

items.q: All 12 sides of this plus shape are 2.5 cm long. What is its perimeter?
items.e: 12 sides × 2.5 cm = 30 cm. 10 cm uses only 4 sides. Count the sides carefully: 3 on each arm, 4 arms.

items.q: What is the perimeter of this shape?
items.e: Add all 8 sides: 4.5 + 7.5 + 9 + 7.5 + 4.5 + 12 + 18 + 12 = 75 m. The notch adds two 7.5 m sides, so the answer is more than the 60 m of a plain 18 m by 12 m rectangle.

items.q: All the corners are square corners. Each notch in this H shape is 6 m wide and 4 m deep. What is the perimeter?
items.e: Count the sides first: 12. Each notch has two 4 m sides and one 6 m side. Add them all: 3 + 4 + 6 + 4 + 3 + 11 + 3 + 4 + 6 + 4 + 3 + 11 = 62 m. 46 m is the rectangle around it, which leaves out the four 4 m sides that go in and out of the notches.

items.q: A corner was cut off a rectangle. What is the perimeter of the new shape?
items.e: Add the 5 sides, including the slanted one: 9 + 5 + 4 + 12 + 8 = 38 cm. 40 cm is the perimeter of the whole rectangle before the corner was cut.

items.q: A corner was cut off a rectangle. What is the perimeter of the new shape?
items.e: Add the 5 sides, including the slanted one: 16 + 9 + 12 + 5 + 6 = 48 m. 50 m is the perimeter of the whole rectangle before the corner was cut.

items.q: A rectangle and a triangle are put together. What is the perimeter of the whole shape?
items.e: Go around the outside only: 8 + 5 + 8 + 5 + 8 = 34 cm. The dashed line is inside the shape, so it is not part of the perimeter. Adding the two perimeters (26 + 24 = 50) counts the inside line twice.

items.q: A rectangle and a triangle are put together. What is the perimeter of the whole shape?
items.e: Go around the outside only: 6.5 + 4.5 + 9 + 4.5 + 6.5 = 31 m. The dashed line is inside the shape, so it is not part of the perimeter. Adding the two perimeters (27 + 22 = 49) counts the inside line twice.

items.q: Two rectangles, each 8 cm by 3 cm, are put end to end so their 3 cm sides touch. They make one long rectangle. What is its perimeter?
items.e: The new rectangle is 8 + 8 = 16 cm long and 3 cm wide: 2 × (16 + 3) = 38 cm. 44 cm adds the two perimeters (22 + 22) and counts the two 3 cm sides that are now inside.

items.q: Five squares with 4 cm sides are put in a row, side by side. What is the perimeter of the row?
items.e: The row is 5 × 4 = 20 cm long and 4 cm tall: 2 × (20 + 4) = 48 cm. 80 cm (5 × 16) counts the sides where the squares touch, which are inside.

items.q: Ethan puts two equilateral triangles with 6 cm sides together along one side. They make a 4-sided shape. What is its perimeter?
items.e: The new shape has 4 outside sides of 6 cm: 4 × 6 = 24 cm. 36 cm adds both triangles (18 + 18) and counts the shared side twice.

items.q: Two regular hexagons with 4 cm sides are joined along one side. What is the perimeter of the new shape?
items.e: 2 hexagons have 12 sides. The joined side is inside, and it hides one side from each hexagon: 12 − 2 = 10 outside sides. 10 × 4 = 40 cm. 44 cm takes away only one of the two hidden sides.

items.q: Three regular hexagons with 5 cm sides are joined in a row like this. What is the perimeter of the whole shape?
items.e: 3 hexagons have 3 × 6 = 18 sides. Each place where two hexagons touch hides 2 sides (one from each), and there are 2 places: 18 − 4 = 14 sides on the outside. 14 × 5 = 70 cm. 90 cm counts every side, even the inside ones.

items.q: A 6 cm square and a 10 cm by 4 cm rectangle are put together. What is the perimeter of the new shape?
items.e: Missing sides: 6 − 4 = 2 cm and 6 + 10 = 16 cm. Add the outside: 6 + 2 + 10 + 4 + 16 + 6 = 44 cm. Adding the two perimeters (24 + 28 = 52) counts the 4 cm dashed side twice, and it is inside the shape.

items.q: All the corners are square corners. The two sides of the notch are the same length. What is the perimeter?
items.e: The notch is 6 cm deep, so its other side is also 6 cm. The bottom of the notch is 14 − 4 − 4 = 6 cm. Add all 8 sides: 4 + 6 + 6 + 6 + 4 + 9 + 14 + 9 = 58 cm. 46 cm adds only the sides with numbers.

items.q: All the corners are square corners. What is the perimeter?
items.e: Going down on the right: 3 + 4 = 7 cm, so going up on the left must also be 7 cm. The missing up side is 7 − 4 = 3 cm. Going right: 6 + 4 = 10 cm, so going left must be 10 cm. The missing side is 10 − 6 = 4 cm. Add all 8 sides: 6 + 3 + 4 + 4 + 6 + 3 + 4 + 4 = 34 cm.

items.q: All the corners are square corners. What is the perimeter of this staircase shape?
items.e: The steps that go across add up to 7.5 m, and the steps that go down add up to 4.5 m. So the perimeter is the same as a 7.5 m by 4.5 m rectangle: 2 × (7.5 + 4.5) = 24 m.

items.q: All the corners are square corners. What is the perimeter of this staircase shape?
items.e: The steps that go across add up to 12 cm, and the steps that go down add up to 9 cm. So the perimeter is the same as a 12 cm by 9 cm rectangle: 2 × (12 + 9) = 42 cm.

items.q: Which shape has the longer perimeter?
items.e: A: 2 × (8 + 5) = 26 cm. B: 8 + 2 + 4 + 3 + 4 + 5 = 26 cm. They are the same. Cutting a corner out of a rectangle moves two sides inward, but their lengths stay the same.

items.q: This arrow is 8 cm across at its widest point. The two ? sides are the same length. What is the perimeter of the arrow?
items.e: The arrowhead is 8 cm across and the shaft is 4 cm across, so the two ? sides share 8 − 4 = 4 cm: 2 cm each. Add all 7 sides: 10 + 2 + 5 + 5 + 2 + 10 + 4 = 38 cm. 34 cm leaves out the two short sides, and 42 cm uses 4 cm for each one.

items.q: Kai says a U-shaped figure has the same perimeter as the 12 cm by 8 cm rectangle around it. The notch in the U is 5 cm deep. What is the real perimeter?
items.e: The rectangle around it has 2 × (12 + 8) = 40 cm. The notch adds two extra sides going in and out: 2 × 5 = 10 cm. 40 + 10 = 50 cm. The shortcut works for an L shape, but not when there is a notch.

items.q: Simran’s family puts a fence around a rectangular vegetable garden in Kelowna. The garden is 14.5 m long and 9 m wide. How much fence do they need?
items.e: 2 × 14.5 + 2 × 9 = 29 + 18 = 47 m. 23.5 m is only two sides, and 130.5 is the area.

items.q: Harjot builds a dog run 15 m long and 8 m wide. It has a gate 1.5 m wide, and the gate is not part of the fence. How much fence does he need?
items.e: Perimeter: 2 × 15 + 2 × 8 = 46 m. Take away the gate: 46 − 1.5 = 44.5 m. 47.5 m adds the gate instead of taking it away.

items.q: A chicken run is built against a barn. The 12 m side runs along the barn wall, so it needs no fence. The run is 6.5 m wide. How much fence is needed for the other 3 sides?
items.e: Fence goes on one 12 m side and two 6.5 m sides: 12 + 6.5 + 6.5 = 25 m. 37 m puts fence along the barn wall too, and 30.5 m uses the wrong side as the wall.

items.q: Owen uses 52 m of fence to go around a rectangular sheep pen. The pen is 15.5 m long. How wide is it?
items.e: Two lengths: 2 × 15.5 = 31 m. 52 − 31 = 21 m for the two widths. 21 ÷ 2 = 10.5 m. 21 m forgets to halve.

items.q: A rectangular field is 30 m long and 18 m wide. Fence posts go all the way around it, 2 m apart, with a post at every corner. How many posts are needed?
items.e: Perimeter: 2 × (30 + 18) = 96 m. One post every 2 m: 96 ÷ 2 = 48 posts. The fence is a closed loop, so the last post is also the first one. 49 would be right for a straight fence.

items.q: Mei’s backyard in Burnaby is L-shaped. All the corners are square corners. How much fence goes all the way around it?
items.e: Missing sides: 18 − 11 = 7 m and 15 − 7 = 8 m. Add all 6 sides: 18 + 7 + 7 + 8 + 11 + 15 = 66 m. Shortcut: 2 × (18 + 15) = 66. 51 m adds only the sides with numbers.

items.q: Fencing costs $12 per metre. Mateo’s garden is a rectangle 10 m long and 6.5 m wide. How much will it cost to fence all the way around?
items.e: Perimeter: 2 × (10 + 6.5) = 33 m. Cost: 33 × $12 = $396. $198 fences only two sides, and $780 uses the area (65) instead of the perimeter.

items.q: A loop hiking trail near Squamish has 4 parts: 1.2 km, 850 m, 1.5 km and 950 m. How long is the whole loop?
items.e: Change to one unit: 850 m = 0.85 km and 950 m = 0.95 km. 1.2 + 0.85 + 1.5 + 0.95 = 4.5 km. 2.7 km adds only the parts in kilometres, and 3.55 km leaves out the 950 m part.

items.q: A gazebo in a Victoria park has a floor shaped like a regular hexagon with 2.4 m sides. A railing goes on every side except one, which is the entrance. How long is the railing?
items.e: A hexagon has 6 sides. The railing is on 5 of them: 5 × 2.4 = 12 m. 14.4 m forgets the entrance.

items.q: A trail around a pond near Kamloops is shaped like a triangle. Its sides are 0.8 km, 1.25 km and 950 m. How long is the trail?
items.e: 950 m = 0.95 km. 0.8 + 1.25 + 0.95 = 3 km. 2.05 km leaves out a side, 2.145 km changes 950 m to 0.095 km by mistake, and 952.05 adds 950 as if it were kilometres.

items.q: Chloe frames a square painting with ribbon. Each side of the painting is 32.5 cm. How much ribbon goes all the way around, in metres?
items.e: 4 × 32.5 = 130 cm. 100 cm = 1 m, so 130 cm = 1.3 m. 130 m forgets to change centimetres to metres.

items.q: Ava jogs 4 times around a soccer field that is 100 m long and 64 m wide. How far does she jog, in kilometres?
items.e: One lap: 2 × (100 + 64) = 328 m. 4 laps: 4 × 328 = 1312 m = 1.312 km. 0.656 km uses only 100 + 64 for each lap.

items.q: For the Terry Fox Run, students run laps of a path around the school field. The field is 110 m long and 65 m wide. How many laps make 3.5 km?
items.e: One lap: 2 × (110 + 65) = 350 m. 3.5 km = 3500 m. 3500 ÷ 350 = 10 laps. 20 laps would be right only if one lap were 110 + 65 = 175 m.

items.q: A hockey rink is about 61 m long and 26 m wide. About how long are the boards all the way around it?
items.e: 2 × 61 + 2 × 26 = 122 + 52 = 174 m. 87 m is one length and one width, and 1586 is the area.

items.q: Ms. Grewal’s bulletin board is 1.8 m long and 1.2 m wide. She has a 5 m roll of paper border. Is it enough to go all the way around?
items.e: Perimeter: 2 × (1.8 + 1.2) = 6 m. 5 < 6, so it is not enough. 3 m is only one length and one width, and 2.16 is the area.

items.q: Garden A is a square with 9 m sides. Garden B is a rectangle 12 m by 5.5 m. Which garden needs more fence?
items.e: A: 4 × 9 = 36 m. B: 2 × (12 + 5.5) = 35 m. 36 − 35 = 1, so A needs 1 m more. 15 compares the areas (81 and 66), not the fences.

items.q: Lucas walks 3 times around a city block in Vancouver. The block is 185 m long and 95 m wide. How far does he walk, in kilometres?
items.e: One time around: 2 × (185 + 95) = 560 m. 3 times: 3 × 560 = 1680 m = 1.68 km. 0.84 km uses only 185 + 95 for each lap.

items.q: A loop trail on Vancouver Island has 5 parts and is 6.4 km long. Four of the parts are 1.5 km, 1.2 km, 0.9 km and 1.6 km. How long is the fifth part?
items.e: Add the parts you know: 1.5 + 1.2 + 0.9 + 1.6 = 5.2 km. Subtract: 6.4 − 5.2 = 1.2 km. 2.8 km leaves out the 1.6 km part.

items.q: A community garden in Surrey is a rectangle. It is twice as long as it is wide, and its perimeter is 84 m. How long is it?
items.e: Width + length = 84 ÷ 2 = 42 m. The length is 2 widths, so 3 widths = 42 m and one width = 14 m. Length = 2 × 14 = 28 m. Check: 2 × (28 + 14) = 84.

items.q: A farm in the Fraser Valley is a rectangle 1.25 km long and 800 m wide. How many metres of fence go all the way around it?
items.e: Change first: 1.25 km = 1250 m. 2 × (1250 + 800) = 2 × 2050 = 4100 m. 1602.5 comes from 2 × 1.25 + 2 × 800, which mixes kilometres and metres. 3300 m leaves out one width.
